Iraklis B.C.|Iraklis Thessaloniki]] | years6 = 2023 | team6 = [[WWU Baskets Münster]] | years7 = 2023–2025 | team7 = [[Keflavík men's basketball|Keflavík]] | years8 = 2025–2026 | team8 = [[Ármann men's basketball|Ármann]] | years9 = 2026–present | team9 = [[SAE Scientifica Legnano]] | highlights = *[[Icelandic Men's Basketball Cup|Icelandic Cup]] (2024) *[[Icelandic Men's Basketball Supercup|Icelandic Super Cup]] (2024) }} '''Marek Doležaj''' (born 13 April 1998) is a Slovak professional basketball player{{cite web | title=Marek Doležaj si necháva čas na dôležité rozhodnutia | website=SLOVENSKÁ BASKETBALOVÁ ASOCIÁCIA | url=https://slovakbasket.sk/sk/article/marek-dolezaj-si-nechava-cas-na-dolezite-rozhodnutia | language=sk | access-date=2024-02-22}} who plays for [[SAE Scientifica Legnano]] in the Italian [[Serie B Basket]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Syracuse Orange men's basketball|Syracuse Orange]]. In 2024, he won the [[Icelandic Men's Basketball Cup|Icelandic Basketball Cup]] as a member of [[Keflavík men's basketball|Keflavík]]. ==Early life== Doležaj was born in [[Bratislava]], the son of Miloš Doležaj, a banker, and Ladislava, a professor. His older sister played volleyball. Doležaj grew up playing soccer but first began playing basketball at the age of seven after a coach suggested it. He studied at the Gymnázium Hubeného in Bratislava. ==Basketball== ===Early career=== Doležaj joined [[MBK Karlovka Bratislava]] of the [[Slovak Basketball League|Extraliga]] in 2014, and averaged 2.1 points and 1.1 rebounds per game. He signed with [[Club Baloncesto El Olivar]] of the Spanish [[LEB Plata]] in October 2015.{{cite web |title=Marek Dolezaj, nueva pieza para el filial y el Júnior del CAI Zaragoza |url=https://www.casademontzaragoza.es/noticias/marek-dolezaj-nueva-pieza-para-el-filial-y-el-j%C3%BAnior-del-cai-zaragoza |website=Casademont Zaragoza |access-date=August 22, 2021 |language=Spanish |date=October 8, 2015}} He put videos of himself playing basketball on YouTube, which attracted the attention of [[Syracuse Orange men's basketball|Syracuse]] assistant coach [[Adrian Autry]]. Autry eventually came to Bratislava to recruit Doležaj.{{cite web |title=Slovak Basketball Player Marek Dolezaj at Syracuse University |url=https://www.fcsu.com/slovak-basketball-player-marek-dolezaj-at-syracuse-university/ |website=First Catholic Slovak Union |access-date=August 22, 2021 |date=March 5, 2020}} During the 2016-17 season, he played for MBK Karlovka Bratislava and averaged 11.7 points and 4.2 rebounds per game. In May 2017, he committed to play college basketball at Syracuse after talking to his best friend Jack, who grew up in Upstate, NY.{{cite news |last1=Ditota |first1=Donna |title=Marek Dolezaj, 6-9 forward from Slovakia, signs with Syracuse basketball |url=https://www.syracuse.com/orangebasketball/2017/05/marek_dolezaj_a_6-9_forward_from_slovakia_has_committed_to_syracuse_basketball.html |access-date=August 22, 2021 |work=[[The Post-Standard]] |date=May 23, 2017}} ===College career=== As a freshman, Doležaj started the final 17 games of the season and averaged 5.8 points and 4.8 rebounds per game, helping the team reach the NCAA Tournament's Sweet 16. He averaged 4.1 points and 3.5 rebounds per game as a sophomore, starting six games.{{cite news |last1=Waters |first1=Mike |title=Syracuse's Marek Dolezaj on 19-point game: 'It's mindset' |url=https://www.syracuse.com/orangebasketball/2019/11/syracuses-marek-dolezaj-on-19-point-game-its-mindset.html |access-date=August 22, 2021 |work=[[The Post-Standard]] |date=November 18, 2019}} On February 1, 2020, Dolezaj scored a career-high 22 points in a 97-88 loss to [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke]].{{cite news |title=No. 9 Duke beats Syracuse 97-88; Carey another double-double |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401168362 |access-date=August 22, 2021 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=February 1, 2020}} As a junior, he averaged 10.4 points and 6.4 rebounds per game. Doležaj was slowed by a broken finger as a senior. He chipped his tooth in a game against [[Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball|Georgetown]] on January 9, 2021.{{cite news |last1=Carlson |first1=Chris |title=Marek Dolezaj isn't supposed to eat pizza for 2 weeks, but Buddy Boeheim believes he will 'find a way' |url=https://www.syracuse.com/orangebasketball/2021/01/marek-dolezaj-isnt-supposed-to-eat-pizza-for-2-weeks-but-buddy-boeheim-believes-he-will-find-a-way.html |access-date=August 22, 2021 |work=[[The Post-Standard]] |date=January 11, 2021}} Doležaj averaged 9.8 points, 5.1 rebounds, and 3.3 assists per game, helping the Orange advance to the NCAA tournament's Sweet 16.{{cite news |last1=Sladek |first1=Tommy |title=SU men's basketball: Marek Dolezaj going pro, won't return next season |url=https://cnycentral.com/sports/college/su-mens-basketball-marek-dolezaj-going-pro-wont-return-next-season |access-date=August 23, 2021 |work=CNY Central |date=April 7, 2021}} He finished his career with 960 points and 649 rebounds. Doležaj declined to accept the NCAA's additional year of eligibility granted due to the COVID-19 pandemic, instead pursuing a professional career.{{cite news |title=Marek Dolezaj says goodbye to Syracuse |url=https://www.localsyr.com/orange-nation/marek-dolezaj-says-goodbye-to-syracuse/ |access-date=August 22, 2021 |work=LocalSyr.com |date=April 7, 2021}}{{cite news |title=NBA announces early entry candidates for NBA Draft 2021 |url=https://www.nba.com/news/nba-announces-early-entry-candidates-for-nba-draft-2021 |access-date=28 September 2024 |work=[[NBA.com]] |date=2 June 2021}} ===Professional career=== On August 17, 2021, Doležaj signed with [[BC Ternopil]] of the [[Ukrainian Basketball SuperLeague]].{{cite news |last1=Waters |first1=Mike |title=Former Syracuse basketball player Marek Dolezaj has signed with a pro team in Europe |url=https://www.syracuse.com/orangebasketball/2021/08/former-syracuse-basketball-player-marek-dolezaj-has-signed-with-a-pro-team-in-europe.html |access-date=August 22, 2021 |work=[[The Post-Standard]] |date=August 17, 2021}} He averaged 9.8 points, 3.5 rebounds, 1.9 assists and 1.1 steals per game. On January 13, 2022, Doležaj signed with [[G.S. Iraklis B.C.|Iraklis]] of the [[Greek Basket League]].{{cite web |last1=Mammides |first1=Chris |title=Marek Dolezaj (ex Ternopil TNEU) joins Iraklis |url=https://www.eurobasket.com/Greece/news/726368/Marek-Dolezaj-(ex-Ternopil-TNEU)-joins-Iraklis |website=Eurobasket |access-date=January 13, 2022 |date=January 13, 2022}} In 13 games, he averaged 4 points and 3.7 rebounds in 23 minutes per contest. In July 2023, Doležaj signed with [[Keflavík men's basketball|Keflavík]] of the Icelandic [[Úrvalsdeild karla (basketball)|Úrvalsdeild karla]].{{cite news |author1=Smári Jökull Jónsson |title=Hávaxinn Slóvaki til liðs við Keflavík |url=https://www.visir.is/g/20232435821d/havaxinn-slovaki-til-lids-vid-keflavik |access-date=5 July 2023 |work=[[Vísir.is]] |date=4 July 2023 |language=Icelandic}} On 23 March 2024, he won the [[Icelandic Men's Basketball Cup|Icelandic Basketball Cup]] with Keflavík.{{cite news |author1=Jóhann Páll Ástvaldsson |author2=Almarr Ormarsson |title=Keflvíkingar bikarmeistarar eftir ótrúlega sveiflu |url=https://www.ruv.is/frettir/ithrottir/2024-03-23-keflvikingar-bikarmeistarar-eftir-otrulega-sveiflu-408336 |access-date=23 March 2024 |work=[[RÚV]] |date=23 March 2024 |language=Icelandic}} On 28 September 2024, he won the [[Icelandic Men's Basketball Supercup|Icelandic Super Cup]] after Keflavík defeated reigning national champions [[Valur men's basketball|Valur]] 98–88 in the cup final.{{cite news |author1=Stefán Marteinn Ólafsson |title=Uppgjörið: Keflavík - Þór Ak. 82-86 - Þór skellti meisturunum |url=https://www.visir.is/g/20242627182d/uppgjorid-keflavik-thor-ak.-82-86-thor-skellti-meisturunum |access-date=28 September 2024 |work=[[Vísir.is]] |date=28 September 2024 |language=Icelandic}} In June 2025, he signed with freshly promoted [[Ármann men's basketball|Ármann]].{{cite news |author1=Hjörtur Leó Guðjónsson |title=Dolezaj til liðs við nýliðana |url=https://www.visir.is/g/20252740279d/dolezaj-til-lids-vid-nylidana |access-date=18 June 2025 |work=[[Vísir.is]] |date=17 June 2025 |language=Icelandic}} For the season he averaged 11.2 points and 6.5 rebounds, helping Ármann avoid relegation. In July 2026 he signed with [[SAE Scientifica Legnano]] in the Italian [[Serie B Basket]].{{cite web |last1=Duchovic |first1=Michal |title=Legnano sign Marek Dolezaj |url=https://www.eurobasket.com/Slovakia/news/1003313/Legnano-sign-Marek-Dolezaj |website=Eurobasket |access-date=July 1, 2026 |date=July 1, 2026}} ==National team career== Doležaj has represented Slovakia in several international competitions. He participated in the [[2015 FIBA Europe Under-18 Championship Division B]], averaging 9.1 points, 9 rebounds and 4 assists per game despite being younger than most players. Doležaj posted a triple double of 11 points, 12 rebounds and 10 assists against Ireland. In the [[2016 FIBA U18 European Championship Division B]], he led the team in scoring and rebounding with 13.4 points, 9.4 rebounds and 1.9 assists per game. Doležaj averaged 11 points, 6.4 rebounds, and 2.4 assists in the [[2018 FIBA U20 European Championship Division B]] qualifiers.{{cite web |title=Marek DOLEZAJ |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/europe/u20b/2018/player/Marek-Dolezaj |website=[[FIBA]] |access-date=August 22, 2021}} ==References== {{Reflist}} ==External links== {{commons category}} *[https://www.korfustatt.is/Leikmadur/301170 Úrvalsdeild statistics] at Körfustatt *[https://cuse.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/marek-dolezaj/19377 Syracuse Orange bio] {{authority control}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Doležaj, Marek}} [[Category:1998 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:Iraklis Thessaloniki B.C. players]] [[Category:Ármann men's basketball players]] [[Category:Keflavík men's basketball players]] [[Category:Power forwards]] [[Category:Basketball players from Bratislava]] [[Category:Slovak expatriate sportspeople in Greece]] [[Category:Slovak expatriate basketball people in Germany]] [[Category:Slovak expatriate basketball people in Spain]] [[Category:Slovak expatriate basketball people in the United States]] [[Category:Slovak men's basketball players]] [[Category:Syracuse Orange men's basketball players]] [[Category:Uni Baskets Münster players]] [[Category:Úrvalsdeild karla (basketball) players]] [[Category:21st-century Slovak sportsmen]]
